newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians condemn new Jerusalem settler plan.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians condemn new Jerusalem settler plan.

text.p: Palestinians on Friday condemned an Israeli decision to build a Jewish settler enclave in the heart of Arab East Jerusalem as a "declaration of war".
Israel's Jerusalem City Council took the decision late on Thursday, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rushed out a statement vowing to prevent the plan from going ahead.

Netanyahu's peace talks with Yasser Arafat's PLO have been in crisis since March when Netanyahu broke ground on Har Homa settlement on a hilltop known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim at the edge of Arab East Jerusalem.

Israel Television said the latest decision would enable Irving Moskowitz, a U.S. Jewish businessman who bankrolls Jewish settlement in occupied areas, to build for Jews in the 11,000-strong Arab neighbourhood of Ras al-Amoud.

"It's a known declaration of war on the Palestinians in East Jerusalem, on the Palestinians in general, and a complete disregard of the spirit of the signed agreement," Arafat's adviser Ahmed Tibi told Israeli army radio.
Saeb Erekat, Arafat's senior negotiator, said the Palestinian Authority had protested to Netanyahu's office insisting that the plan be scrapped.
Yossi Sarid, head of the leftist Meretz party in Israel's parliament, forecast an outburst of violence.

He likened the decision to Netanyahu's opening of a tourist tunnel entrance near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem last September which sparked clashes and gun battles that took the lives of 61 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers.

"I am really certain that the building in Ras al-Amoud is the match that will light the great fire in the territories, a great fire that will burn lives of both Jews and Arabs," Sarid, a former peace negotiator, told Israel Radio.

Israel's Jerusalem municipal planning commission gave conditional approval last December to a plan for 132 settler homes in Ras al-Amoud. The plan required the approval of Interior Minister Eli Suissa but was later shelved.

Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert said the plan given the green light on Thursday was for a scaled-down project on the same land east of Jerusalem's walled Old City. A spokeswoman said this plan had received all relevant approvals years ago.
"We are fighting over Jerusalem here and one can imagine there are elements who don't like that," Olmert said.
Netanyahu's office said it would work to prevent the plan's implementation. It said it was the wrong time for such a project when talks with the Palestinians were in crisis.
"There are means by which the government can prevent this building...It can invoke a national interest and security reasons," said his communications chief David Bar-Illan.
"So I presume that...there are ways for the government to prevent the building there," he told Reuters.
Miami-based Moskowitz is said to own the 3.5 acre (1.4 hectare) plot in Ras al-Amoud. The claim is disputed by Palestinian officials.
Ras al-Amoud residents themselves vented their fears.

"Every time we build all our aspirations and dreams that this peace process is going to bring us self-stability, to live in dignity and peace, the Israelis demolish these aspirations," said Ahmad Ali, a 37-year-old taxi driver.
The status of East Jerusalem is one of the most volatile issues dividing Israelis and Palestinians. The PLO wants East Jerusalem as capital of a future Palestinian state.
Israel, which occupied East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East War, says both sides of the city form its "united and eternal" capital.
Palestinians say Israeli moves in East Jerusalem are aimed at pre-empting peace talks on the city's fate. Some 160,000 Jews have settled in East Jerusalem since 1967. About 155,000 Arabs live there.
Olmert said he doubted Moskowitz would go ahead soon with the plan as approved because the American, who had threatened legal action, would fight to carry out the larger project.
